search_strategy: Methodical but narrow. The agent used four channels: (1) BookStack /api/search for 5-6 exact terms, all near-misses because the design decisions were never given page titles matching those terms; (2) IMAP keyword search over ~8 fixed terms (planner, plan_batches, payload, batch_size, sidecar, plan_id, plan_document, planner again) which found both relevant mail threads (70-76, 80-86) but never expanded to terms that would have caught the 'Week of Jun 9 recap' thread's actual content (l12, listed but never opened) or the 'resumed batch run double-submitted' thread (l6, never found by any search term used); (3) Mattermost full-text search (mmsearch.py) for ~15 terms across several rounds, which was the single most productive tool, surfacing roughly half of all r1 clues and most r2 clues, but the agent leaned on grep-with-context over pre-dumped channel files rather than re-running mmsearch with new terms drawn from what it had just read (e.g. it never searched 'envelope', 'PLAN_FORMAT_VERSION', 'plan_fingerprint', 'batches[0]', or 'top level'), which is why concrete fixture and shape remarks (say22, say24, say25, l1... err l3, l5, l9, l15, l16, l2/l9 covered below) were never found even though they use nearby vocabulary; (4) wiki — the agent DID follow the ticket's explicit advice to fetch pages whole for comments, writing a script that fetches /api/pages/{id} and iterates d.get('comments',[]) for all 114 pages (ids 7-120) in one bulk pass. That pass printed zero '--- COMMENT' lines for any page in the entire corpus, and the agent concluded 'No planner mentions in wiki bodies/comments' (line 2477) without sanity-checking the fetch against a page known to carry comments. This is a silent tooling failure, not a genuine absence, and it specifically cost both wiki-only remarks (g1.r1.l2, g1.r2.l9) on the one page (docs/design/batch-job-status-persistence-across-process-restarts.md) the answer key names as carrying them.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally: commit 71b29d7 merged to main, Gitea Actions CI green, release deployed and verified (lines 5055-5065). The 0.6 reward reflects a genuinely graded but incomplete implementation, not an infra failure.
notable: Line 1170 and line 1939: the agent explicitly and repeatedly judged the entire g1.r1 sidecar (plan_document/plan_fingerprint/PLAN_FILE_NAME/batch_plan.json) to be 'a distractor'/'a serialization subsystem that doesn't exist in the repo', despite having just read two full mail threads and several chat fragments that describe it in concrete, buildable detail (file name, first-key ordering, hash recipe, envelope shape, fixture values). This single judgment call is the root cause of all four g1.r1 fact losses.

Lines 2226-2477: the wiki 'fetch pages whole for comments' script the agent wrote itself, following the ticket's own hint that BookStack search does not index comments, never actually printed a single comment for any of the 114 pages it fetched — a silent bug (comments field structure mismatch or an endpoint quirk) that the agent never caught because it never checked its own script's output against a known-good page.

Lines 1748 and 2008: everywhere the agent DID act (the max_batches_per_plan ceiling, the BatchPlanTooFragmentedError subclassing decision, the per-row-oversize-first ordering, and the sweep-after-plan-succeeds ordering) it reproduced the corpus's exact reasoning, quoting Slack lines almost verbatim in its own code comments and docstrings — the search-and-synthesis process worked well for r2 and for r1's failure_behavior fact; it simply never got applied to r1's sidecar because of the early dismissal.

Lines 1076/1104 and message 102: the agent's IMAP search surfaced 8 'payload' hits including message 102 ('Re: Week of Jun 9 recap: bulk inference fix', which carries the BatchLimits/dataclasses.asdict/max_batches_per_plan envelope spec, i.e. g1.r1.l12) by subject line only, and never opened it with mget.py — a plain missed follow-up, independent of the sidecar-dismissal issue.

The agent's own sanity-check script (lines 3282-3294) independently reproduces several of the exact numeric fixtures the corpus specifies (payload_bytes, the [10]*7 fingerprint input, the 307/307/153 byte split, err.num_batches==3/err.limit==2) — showing it was capable of exactly the kind of close verification the grader rewards, but applied that discipline only to the parts of the ticket it still believed were in scope.
